verses.1: But God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and livestock that were with him in the ark. God caused a wind to blow over the earth, and the waters began to recede.
verses.2: The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens were closed, and the rain stopped falling from the sky.
verses.3: The waters receded steadily from the earth. At the end of 150 days the waters had gone down.
verses.4: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
verses.5: The waters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible.
verses.6: After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
verses.7: and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth.
verses.8: Then he sent out a dove to see if the waters had receded from the surface of the ground.
verses.9: But the dove found nowhere to land because there was still water over all the surface of the earth. So it returned to Noah in the ark. He reached out his hand and took it and brought it back inside.
verses.10: He waited seven more days and again sent the dove out from the ark.
verses.11: When the dove returned to him in the evening, there in its beak was a freshly plucked olive leaf. Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth.
verses.12: He waited seven more days and sent the dove out again, and this time it did not return to him.
verses.13: By the first day of the first month of Noah's six hundred and first year, the water had dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.
verses.14: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month the earth was completely dry.
verses.16: "Come out of the ark, you and your wife and your sons and your sons' wives.
verses.17: Bring out every living creature that is with you — the birds, the animals, and every creature that moves along the ground — so they can multiply on the earth and be fruitful and increase in number."
verses.18: So Noah came out, together with his sons and his wife and his sons' wives.
verses.19: All the animals and all the creatures that move along the ground and all the birds — everything that moves on the earth — came out of the ark, one kind after another.
verses.20: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD and took some of every clean animal and every clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
verses.21: The LORD smelled the pleasing aroma and said in His heart, "Never again will I curse the ground because of mankind, even though every inclination of the human heart is evil from childhood. And never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done.
verses.22: As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never cease."

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
